chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abī Usāmah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Seek refuge in Allah from the assaults of Allah by night and day.
He said: I said to him, “And what are the assaults of Allah?” He said, “The seizing for acts of disobedience.”

key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah, the One from whom refuge is sought and whose punishment is feared
key_terms.الْأَخْذُ: The act of seizing or taking to account
key_terms.سَطَوَاتِ: Sudden assaults or overpowering acts of seizing

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean by seeking refuge from the assaults of Allah by night and day?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches believers to seek refuge in Allah from His sudden punishment at all times, day and night. It explains that these divine assaults mean Allah's seizing of people on account of their sins and acts of disobedience. The narration serves as a warning against persistence in maʿāṣī and encourages constant vigilance and repentance.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Abu Asama, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
Seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from the Assaults of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> by the night and the day’.
I said, ‘And what are the Assaults of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Seizing upon the disobedience’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from ibn ‘Usamah who has said the following:
‘Seek refuge with Allah from His striking you at night or during the day.’
I (the narrator) asked him, ‘What is Allah’s striking?’ The Imam said, ‘It is Allah’s punishing for sins.’”
